properties.description:
`crates/reflow2-core/tests/granularity.rs` — two checks holding `con:granularity-reads-scale-with-artifacts-not-edges`, both COUNTS rather than durations.

`the_reading_costs_one_store_read_per_artifact_plus_a_constant` runs at 10, 40 and 120 artifacts and asserts total reads ≤ N + 2, plus `get_node == 0`. Three sizes, because a budget checked at one size cannot tell a constant from a coefficient.

`adding_edges_does_not_cost_the_reading_anything` is the one that makes the budget mean something: it quadruples the edges while holding the artifacts fixed and asserts the read count is UNCHANGED. The old shape would have quadrupled it. Without this, a budget that happened to pass at one density would look healthy while the defect it forbids was still present.

⚠️ A COUNT, DELIBERATELY, NOT A CLOCK. A duration assertion in a parallel suite measures machine contention, and the standing response is to raise the threshold until it stops complaining — which retires the gate without anybody deciding to. Per-read cost was also measured FLAT (58.0µs over 2853 nodes against 55.1µs over 199), so what the module controls is how many times it asks, not how long each ask takes.

MEASURED BOTH WAYS. Reverting the fix — putting the per-edge `get_node` back — fails both checks and names the constraint in the message ("10 artifacts: 32 reads against a budget of 12"). Restoring it passes 14 of 14. A guard that has only ever been seen green is indistinguishable from one that cannot fail.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK: wall-clock time, deliberately. The change halved the reads and moved the clock not at all (~201ms to ~216ms, noise), because a scan returning 199 nodes costs about what 199 point lookups cost. The budget buys a structural property and buys no speed, and it would be dishonest to guard it with a timer.
properties.findings:
2026-08-21: 14 of 14 granularity tests pass, including both budget checks. Measured on reflow2's own design (2853 nodes, 218 artifacts) via `CountingRead`:

  BEFORE   552 reads   1 scan_nodes, 333 get_node, 218 outgoing   ~201ms
  AFTER    220 reads   2 scan_nodes,   0 get_node, 218 outgoing   ~216ms
  BUDGET   220 (N+2, N=218)

AT BUDGET, so the work STOPPED. Two changes, measured separately: replacing the per-edge `get_node` type-check with one `scan_nodes(Capability)` took 552 → 227, still over; keeping the artifact nodes from the scan already performed rather than re-reading the seven flagged ones took 227 → 220, exactly at budget. Under budget means stop, even though a third change is visible.

⭐ THE CLOCK DID NOT MOVE AND THAT IS THE HONEST RESULT. Reads more than halved; wall time went from ~201ms to ~216ms, which is noise. A `scan_nodes` returning 199 nodes costs about what 199 point lookups cost, so this bought the structural property — cost scales with what the reading reports on — and bought no speed. The budget said so in advance, which is the whole reason for writing it first.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNDONE: the 218 `outgoing` calls, one per artifact. Removing them needs a bulk edge-scan the storage contract does not offer, so it would mean changing dynograph-foundation's API — another repo. At budget, so it stops here rather than reaching across that boundary.

AND THE REAL SPEED TARGET IS ELSEWHERE, UNMEASURED: `graph_report` costs ~78s in the same configuration against granularity's ~216ms. Granularity is 0.3% of it. Nothing here touches that, and optimising granularity for wall clock would have been manufacturing work.
properties.name: The reading costs one store read per artifact plus a constant, and adding edges costs it nothing
